reviewed_contracts: All eighteen held file bodies, generated-wrapper emitter, four templates, packaging/examples/docs and authored generation/JavaScript models were read. Actual Rust/TinyGo/JavaScript/AssemblyScript SDK methods, error names, signatures, full-width event fields and canonical component APIs were cross-checked as source.

No alias is inferred from a type. Distinct explicit role aliases open before server advertisement; partial construction/activation failure closes acquired roles and preserves the original failure plus cleanup results. No rollback revocation, implicit native networking, clock, thread or automatic retry is introduced.

Synchronous service uses one actual service_call. Asynchronous service uses the existing real submit primitive and separate fresh exclusive observer, finite pending IDs, existing unified envelope decoder, backend/source/instance/session/next-sequence checks and owned correlation. Only validated response or matched numeric terminal error retires pending ID; malformed/foreign/retired-source metadata cannot publish a typed value.

Four independent action roles plus explicit fifth cancel-any role remain distinct. Own cancellation requires a locally admitted nonzero ID. Cancel-all zero is accepted only with stronger role. Cancellation ACK retains goal; complete matching-ID feedback retains it; only decoded terminal kinds2..4 retire it. Custom generated goal/result/feedback codecs are used directly rather than builtin Fibonacci factories.

Incoming servers admit only complete decoded nonzero unique tickets into finite local tables. Host principal/deadline/revocation checks remain authoritative. Successful service/terminal response retires exact ID; feedback and refused encoding/import retain it.

Private per-facade owner state and callback lease guard nested polling/dispatch/close/revoke before dequeue or retirement. Exact response operations remain usable in Action handler; service callback must return a value and must not also manually respond. JS finally spans await; Rust Rc/Cell RAII pass has no borrowed-owner lifetime overlap with server mutation; TinyGo copied facades share pointer state and defer clears normal/panic path; AssemblyScript documents fatal-trap limitation.

Template filenames are closed literal generator inputs, bounded-read with exact bytes/SHA and re-read before output commit. Non-RPC message-only source products retain existing count/bodies and do not read templates. Four additive files produce RPC guest12/native15 without changing C/C++/record emitters.

Examples preserve actual package/module imports, selected real backend and explicit user-owned scheduling/checked cleanup. Documentation accurately distinguishes capability ABI API from native rclcpp/rclpy source compatibility and preparation-only guest catalogs from actual bound native identities.
remaining_actual_checks: Root review/apply into a new complete immutable source freeze and actual guarded controls.
Execute the authored generation/model suites under Root64GiB guard; models are not native ROS/Runtime evidence.
Compile all four generated language modules/examples for their real Wasm toolchains and validate imports, memories and embedded JavaScript module map.
Run actual positive/default-denied custom Service/Action interactions, including real observer admission, callback lease/rollback/terminal correlation and checked cleanup.
documented_API_limits: Rust Backend exposes ABI version but no ROS numeric selector independent of consumer Cargo features; explicit actual Backend is required and native grants bind authority; async envelope version is checked.
TinyGo backend is selected by the existing exact ros1/ros2 build tags, not by an invented runtime selector.
JavaScript requires a real fixed-capacity Session/CopiedTransport and an explicit complete embedded module map; it creates no networking implementation.
AssemblyScript fatal abort/trap cannot promise lease cleanup; all normal paths release local busy state.
performed: Read source and actual SDK APIs
not_performed: Compiler, Runtime, ROS or QEMU execution
